app.title: BasinLens CCS
app.summary: A person uploads a table of candidate scenarios, or uses the bundled synthetic ones. Each input is given as a low, most-likely and high value. They set the number of Monte Carlo samples and a random seed, and the app simulates a capacity distribution for each scenario. It also scores each scenario with a weighted heuristic attention score. An overview table lists every scenario's Q10/Q50/Q90 and attention category. The person then picks one scenario to see its quantile metrics, its sampled distribution, how strongly each uncertain input drives the result, and the parts of its attention score. Finally they download the summary as a CSV.

task.text: Turn uncertain input ranges for each candidate into a simulated distribution of an output quantity with sensitivities and a transparent flag score, so candidates can be compared and investigation needs noted.

data.text: A table of candidate scenarios. Each uncertain input has a low, most-likely and high estimate, and each scenario has a few single-valued screening indicators. Monte Carlo samples are generated from these.
data.item: a candidate storage-site scenario with triangular estimates for its inputs and point values for its screening indicators

stage.text: early concept screening of candidate sites from assumed input ranges, before detailed simulation or site characterisation

mechanism.text: Sidebar run settings (upload, sample count, seed) drive a recomputation that fills an overview table of all scenarios. A selectbox opens one scenario in a detail area with quantile metrics, a histogram, a sensitivity bar chart and an attention-component bar chart, and a button exports the summary table.

field.text: Monte Carlo volumetric storage-capacity screening in geologic CO2 storage

workflow.name: estimate an uncertain quantity for each candidate by simulation and flag candidates for follow-up

steps.here: Upload a CSV of site scenarios with low/mode/high columns per input, or fall back to three synthetic sites. Validation errors name the field and row and stop the run.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: A slider sets the Monte Carlo samples per site and a number input sets the seed. Each site's capacity M = A·h·φ·ρCO₂·E is sampled from triangular inputs and summarised as Q10/Q50/Q90, alongside a weighted attention score.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: The overview table lists every site's Q10/Q50/Q90 capacity, attention score and category, sorted by increasing attention and then decreasing Q50.
The 'Inspect a site' selectbox shows that site's Q10/Q50/Q90 metrics and a histogram of its simulated capacity with the median marked.

steps.step: see which inputs drive the result
steps.here: A horizontal bar chart ranks the five uncertain inputs by their rank correlation with simulated capacity.

steps.step: break a flag score into its components
steps.here: Shows the attention category and total out of 100, with a bar for each indicator: caprock thickness, fault proximity and legacy-well density.
'Download summary CSV' saves the full summary table, including attention components and the mean and SD of capacity.

distinctive: Each input is a triangular low/most-likely/high estimate, so the result is a distribution summarised by Q10/Q50/Q90 rather than a single number.
The seed and sample count are user-set and per-site seeds follow input order, which makes runs reproducible.
Rank-correlation sensitivity shows which assumed input range drives each site's uncertainty.
Containment questions are kept apart from capacity: a separate weighted heuristic score with visible linear thresholds is labelled as an attention indicator, not a risk probability.
Physical bounds are enforced on input: fractions must be in [0,1], other inputs non-negative, and IDs unique and non-empty, with field-specific errors.
